raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`EnvField.override` does not restore the environment variable when the `with` body raises. It snapshots the previous presence, value and `_set_to_none` state, then restores them after the `yield`, so an exception propagating out of the block skips the restore entirely and the override leaks into the rest of the process.

That is the opposite of the documented contract. `.claude/skills/env-var-conventions/SKILL.md` tells callers to prefer `override` over touching `os.environ` precisely because it "restores the original cleanly, including the explicit-None state, even if the block raises", and lists it as the supported way to scope a value in tests and to seed a `subprocess.Popen`. The sibling context manager `ParallelContext.override` in `runtime_context.py` already restores in a `finally`.

Reproduction, CPU only, on `dba22e9b68`:

```python
import os
from sglang.srt.environ import envs

name = envs.SGLANG_IS_IN_CI.name
os.environ.pop(name, None)

try:
    with envs.SGLANG_IS_IN_CI.override(True):
        raise RuntimeError("boom")
except RuntimeError:
    pass

print(name in os.environ, envs.SGLANG_IS_IN_CI.get())
# main:     True True
# expected: False False
```

Two places this bites:

Tests. 82 files under `test/registered/unit/` alone scope an env var with `envs.*.override(...)`. When a test fails inside one of those blocks, the override survives into every later test in the same process, so one real failure turns into a run of unrelated ones and the root cause is no longer the first red test. `ExitStack` composition, which the conventions doc recommends for multiple overrides, inherits the same hole.

Runtime. `dflash_worker_v2.py:836` wraps a sampling-peak measurement in `with envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_GRAPH_POOL_BORROW.override(False):`, and line 843 reads `graph_pool_borrow_enabled()` immediately after. If the measurement raises, graph-pool borrowing stays disabled for the remaining lifetime of the process.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: wrap the `yield` in `try`/`finally`. The restore block is unchanged and the clean-exit path behaves exactly as before.

`test/registered/unit/test_environ.py`: one case added to `TestEnvField`, beside the existing `test_override_restores_previous_state`, which only covered the clean exit. It walks the three prior states the restore branches on: key absent, key set to a value, and key explicitly set to `None`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no kernel or model forward code is touched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: the change adds a `try`/`finally` around an existing `yield`, with no extra work on the clean path.

## Test Results

```
# the new case, on dba22e9b68 (pre-fix)
FAILED test/registered/unit/test_environ.py::TestEnvField::test_override_restores_state_when_block_raises
AssertionError: True is not false
1 failed, 11 passed

# the new case, with this PR
12 passed

# every unit file that scopes an env var with envs.*.override(...), 82 files
pytest $(grep -rl 'envs\.[A-Z_]*\.override(' test/registered/unit --include='*.py')
pre-fix:  230 failed, 2040 passed, 179 skipped, 13 errors, 3200 subtests passed
with fix: 229 failed, 2041 passed, 179 skipped, 13 errors, 3200 subtests passed
```

The two failure sets differ by exactly one entry, the new test moving from failed to passed. No other test changes state in either direction. The remaining failures and collection errors are identical before and after, and are GPU and platform dependencies unavailable in my local environment.

`isort`, `ruff check --select=F401,F821,F823,UP037`, `ruff format` and `codespell` are clean on both changed files.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not applicable: this makes the code match the behavior already documented in `env-var-conventions`.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. Not applicable, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -98,12 +98,14 @@ def override(self, value: Any):
         backup_value = os.environ.get(self.name)
         backup_set_to_none = self._set_to_none
         self.set(value)
-        yield
-        if backup_present:
-            os.environ[self.name] = backup_value
-        else:
-            os.environ.pop(self.name, None)
-        self._set_to_none = backup_set_to_none
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            if backup_present:
+                os.environ[self.name] = backup_value
+            else:
+                os.environ.pop(self.name, None)
+            self._set_to_none = backup_set_to_none
 
     def clear(self):
         os.environ.pop(self.name, None)

@@ -53,6 +53,28 @@ def test_override_restores_previous_state(self):
         self.assertTrue(envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.is_set())
         self.assertIsNone(envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.get())
 
+    def test_override_restores_state_when_block_raises(self):
+        """An exception leaving the with block must not leak the override: the
+        key's previous presence, value and explicit-None state are restored."""
+        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+            with envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.override(True):
+                raise RuntimeError("boom")
+        self.assertFalse(envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.is_set())
+        self.assertIs(envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.get(), False)
+
+        envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.set(False)
+        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+            with envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.override(True):
+                raise RuntimeError("boom")
+        self.assertIs(envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.get(), False)
+
+        envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.set(None)
+        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
+            with envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.override(True):
+                raise RuntimeError("boom")
+        self.assertTrue(envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.is_set())
+        self.assertIsNone(envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.get())
+
     def test_override_with_exit_stack(self):
         envs.SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT.set(None)
         exit_stack = ExitStack()
